data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's distinguishing criterion—covariance of panel errors with checklist-irrelevant, outcome-relevant features—fails when a checklist omits an expert-unique cue but no observable proxy for that cue is recorded in the evaluation. The residual analogy presupposes the omitted variable is available to test against; if the omitted cue is latent or unmeasured, the covariance is untestable in a single evaluation, leaving no way to distinguish compliance-tracking from genuine coverage in exactly the cases where the expert's cue-set exceeds the checklist.
